43993738.article_content:
Tesla
Tesla has yet to start testing its robotaxi service without driver weeks before launch
Fred Lambert
| May 14 2025 - 5:06 pm PT
171 Comments
Tesla has reportedly yet to start testing its robotaxi service in Austin without a safety driver behind the wheel – just weeks before the planned launch.
For months now, Tesla and CEO Elon Musk have been hyping the launch of “Tesla Robotaxi”, a Uber-like ride-hailing service powered by autonomous Tesla vehicles, starting with a launch in Austin, Texas in June.
We have extensively reported that
this launch is disappointing compared to what Tesla promised for years
: that all its consumer vehicles built since 2016 are capable of self-driving.
Instead, Tesla plans to build an internal fleet of “10-20” Model Ys and have them offer ride-hailing services in a geo-fenced area around Austin, Texas, helped by human teleoperations. This is very similar to what Waymo has been offering in other cities for years, specifically in Austin, for months now.
Advertisement - scroll for more content
Even with the significant downgrade in self-driving capabilities promised with this project, there are many doubts about Tesla’s ability to achieve the lesser goal.
That’s because the robotaxi service will be based on Tesla’s ‘Supervised Full Self-Driving’ program, which is currently achieving about 500 miles between critical disengagements fleet-wide, according to
the latest crowdsourced data
.
Tesla will be able to improve on that by optimizing a version for the geo-fenced area in Austin and it has been training its neural nets for that for months with vehicles going around Austin.
However, a new report now claims that Tesla has yet to start testing its service without safety drivers at the wheel – similar to Tesla’s public ‘Supervised FSD’.
The Information
wrote in a new report:
Elon Musk’s deadline for launching Tesla’s first robotaxi service, in Austin, Texas, is weeks away, but the company hadn’t started testing its cars without a human safety driver as of last month, according to an engineer close to the testing and a former employee. That’s a crucial step required before Tesla can launch the pilot service for customers.
For comparison, before launching its paid ride service in Austin, Waymo tested its vehicles with safety drivers in the area for 6 months and then without safety drivers for another 6 months.
Waymo has now taken over a significant market share of ride-hailing rides in the Texas capital, but it still has limitations; for example, it doesn’t drive on the interstate.
The report also mentions that Tesla has been working with local emergency services in Austin to develop intervention plans in order to avoid causing issues if its autonomous vehicles fail.
Electrek’s Take
Top comment by
Pilar Ackerman
Liked by 12 people
The Tesla faithful don't care if Elon misses his promised dates. He's been missing them for a decade plus and it hasn't impacted the stock price at all. My guess is that falling sales WILL impact the stock price, sooner rather than later.  Though Elon, ever the huckster, will do his best to spin his failures as a success and make even more unfulfilled promises.
View all comments
This is the biggest softball goal. It’s a fraction of what was promised, it’s something that others have achieved before. It’s a punt created for Tesla to finally get a “win” in self-driving.
If they can’t even make it, it would be disastrous, but at least, I hope that it will finally open the eyes of many Tesla shareholders to the reality that Tesla is actually behind in autonomous driving and that Musk’s latest claims that Tesla will have “millions of robotaxi on the road” in 2026 are just the same as when he claimed it would happen in 2025, 2024, 2023, 2022, 2021, 2020, and 2019:
corporate puffery
.
My main concern now is for public safety. I have little hope of US regulators being able to stop Tesla considering Trump is firing anyone who got in Musk’s way after he gave him over $250 million.
If Tesla brings its cowboy approach to this, it could get bad quickly.

data.title: The Internet 1997–2021
data.author: smusamashah
data.article_summary: 这篇文章简要介绍了互联网从1997年到2021年的惊人发展，重点是通过路由表数据展示其增长。文章提到的视频从1997年开始，利用俄勒冈大学的RouteViews项目数据，展示了互联网的扩展过程，并根据企业合并、收购和品牌变化更新网络名称。2010年的地图首次使用BGP数据替代原始traceroute数据，通过颜色展示连接点的活跃程度。2003年的地图则是首次使用全彩和图形逻辑制作，通过不同颜色展示全球各地区的IP分配。文章还提供了多个版本的原始文件和图像供查看。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：互联网早期发展及变迁

不同观点：
• **andrehacker**：认为1997年的互联网规模较小，无需谷歌，用户可以通过1200页的“互联网黄页”书籍查找信息。随后由于书籍形式不可持续，转为了CD-ROM版本。给出了相关存档链接支持其观点。
• **sedatk**：认为1997年是个有趣的起点，因为那时土耳其的ISP开始向公众提供互联网接入，并且国家补贴了拨号上网的费用，推动了互联网的普及。他分享了个人经历，包括在IRC上聊天、下载资料、浏览网页和玩MUD游戏。
• **zetalyrae**：将标题解读为一种“讣告”，可能暗示对过去互联网时代结束的感慨。
• **hous68**：提到Peacock Maps在1999年发布了一张名为“The Whole Internet”的海报，并给出了一个链接展示类似的早期互联网地图。
• **calini**：认为标题像是对前AI和前ChatGPT时代互联网的悼念，但很高兴发现内容其实是一些漂亮的色彩图示。
• **Animats**：指出2021年的互联网需要更新，尤其是考虑到中国IPv6的兴起，并质疑数据收集能否覆盖中国国内的流量情况。
• **aa-jv**：分享了自己在1994年参与创办一家大型ISP的经历，描述了早期互联网的狂野和混乱，尤其是发现大部分流量是成人内容后，对互联网商业活动失去兴趣并离开。

补充讨论：
• **互联网早期形式**：多个评论提到了互联网早期的不同形式，如黄页书籍、CD-ROM和海报地图，展示了互联网在搜索引擎普及前的不同信息组织方式。
• **互联网普及的地区差异**：sedatk提到土耳其互联网的普及得益于国家补贴，展示了不同地区互联网发展的时间和方式差异。
• **互联网内容与商业化**：aa-jv的评论引发了对早期互联网内容和商业化的讨论，尤其是成人内容对互联网发展的影响。
• **技术进步与互联网变迁**：Animats提到IPv6和中国的互联网发展，强调了技术进步和地区差异对互联网的影响。

争议焦点：
• **互联网早期是否更“纯净”**：一些评论（如calini和aa-jv）对早期互联网持有不同的情感，有人怀念过去的时光，而有人则对早期内容和商业化持批评态度。

The Internet 2010
This image was never released publicly prior to 2014. It has only been viewable at the Museum of Modern Art (MoMA) in New York, and in an edition of Discover Magazine. It is the first version of the image rendered using BGP as the data points rather than raw traceroutes. This is a large departure from the original traceroute images, and as a result, provides a framework for future and past images based on the Route Views table dump archive.  The color selection is based on the color of incandescence, where the most connection points represent the highest temperatures in terms of colors of light.​

The Internet 2003
This is our first full Internet map with color and other graphing logic. RFC1918 addresses have been hashed into a unique checksum so they do not incorrectly overlap with other routers or hosts. The checksums resolve to the same host each time to be sure that all routes connect correctly. Another bit of code also removed the routing loops that made a rather large mess out of previous maps. data.title: A Tiny Boltzmann Machine
data.author: anomancer
data.article_summary: Boltzmann Machines是1980年代引入的生成型AI模型，用于无监督学习，可以从数据中学习而无需明确指示。它们由可见和隐藏神经元组成，通过能量函数进行训练，目标是最小化训练数据的能量。一般Boltzmann Machine神经元间全连接，训练复杂度高。Restricted Boltzmann Machine（RBM）则限制可见与隐藏神经元间的连接，训练更快。RBM通过对比散度（Contrastive Divergence）方法训练，包括钳制可见单元、采样隐藏单元、更新权重等步骤。最终，RBM可以从学习到的分布中生成与训练数据类似的新数据。文章还提供了一个浏览器中运行的RBM模拟器以展示训练过程。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于Boltzmann机器及其相关模型、历史、技术细节的讨论

不同观点：
• Nevermark提出了一种新的模型概念"Unbiased-Architecture Instant Boltzmann Model" (UA-IBM)，并讨论了量子计算在模型选择中的潜在应用。他设想利用量子系统在超position状态下测试所有可能的参数和架构，以找到最佳模型。
• dr_dshiv讨论了Boltzmann机器的历史，指出Harmonium（由Smolensky提出）是第一个限制性Boltzmann机器，但其优化目标是“和谐”而非“能量最小化”。他也提到了Hinton和Smolensky的不同研究路径。
• itissid提出了关于Gibbs采样在计算权重更新中的必要性问题，而不是使用今天神经网络中常见的基于梯度的前向和后向传递。

补充讨论：
• sitkack分享了一篇关于David Ackley的文章，并将讨论引向T2 Tile项目。
• oac分享了一个关于RBM训练的可视化视频，唤起对过去研究的回忆。
• thingamarobert提到自己的博士研究基于RBMs，并指出这些模型在AI发展中的重要性，尽管现在已不常被提及。
• nonrandomstring回忆了1990年用C语言构建Boltzmann机器和Perceptrons的经历，描述了当时的AI应用。
• nayuki对文章中的术语准确性提出异议，指出对Restricted Boltzmann Machine的描述应更精确，强调可见神经元和隐藏神经元内部无连接。
• vanderZwan和tomrod对文章的用户体验和拼写错误提出了建议。
• nickvec希望能够调整模拟运行的速度。
• rollulus以幽默的方式引用了Boltzmann Brain的概念，提出了对现实感知的哲学问题。
• bbstats请求文章的存档链接。
• antidumbass报告了在iOS设备上阅读文章时的格式问题。

争议焦点：
• 对Boltzmann机器及其变种的技术细节和历史有不同角度的讨论，特别是在模型优化目标和术语使用上的细微差别。
• 用户体验方面的问题，如页面滚动敏感度和文本显示错误。

总体来看，讨论涵盖了技术细节、历史背景、实际应用和用户体验等多方面内容。

Message from the Author
LiveSplat was developed as a small part of a larger proprietary VR telerobotics system. I posted a video of the Gaussian splatting component of this system on Reddit and many people expressed an interest in experimenting with it themselves. So I spun it out and I'm making it publicly available as LiveSplat (see installation instructions below).
LiveSplat should be considered alpha quality. I do not have the resources to test the installation on many different machines, so let me know if the application does not run on yours (assuming your machine meets the requirements).
I've decided to keep LiveSplat closed source in order to explore potential business opportunities. If you are a business wanting to license/integrate this technology, please email
mark@axby.cc
.
I hope you have fun with LiveSplat!
— Mark Liu

data.article_summary:
**llm-min.txt: 技术文档的Min.js风格压缩用于LLM上下文**

**简介**  
llm-min.txt是一个社区驱动的项目，旨在解决AI编码助手（如GitHub Copilot）因“知识截止”导致无法获取最新库信息的难题。传统方法如llms.txt和Context7存在文件过大或不透明的问题。

**llm-min.txt的创新**  
受JavaScript中min.js文件启发，llm-min.txt通过AI提炼技术文档，生成高度浓缩、结构化的摘要，专为AI优化而非人类阅读。该文件采用结构化知识格式（SKF），包含头部元数据和三大核心部分：定义、用法和关系。

**SKF格式关键元素**  
1. **头部元数据**：包括格式标识、文档来源、生成时间、主命名空间等。
2. **核心部分**：
   - **定义部分**：描述库的静态组件，如类、方法、属性等。
   - **用法部分**：包含代码示例和使用说明。
   - **关系部分**：展示组件间的动态关系，如继承或接口实现。

**优势**  
llm-min.txt通过精简文档，使AI助手能在有限上下文窗口内高效处理最新技术信息，同时保持高准确性。

**未来计划**  
项目计划进一步优化格式和处理流程，并欢迎社区贡献。

**许可**  
该项目采用MIT许可。

What is
llm-min.txt
and Why is it Important?
If you've ever used an AI coding assistant (like GitHub Copilot, Cursor, or others powered by Large Language Models - LLMs), you've likely encountered situations where they don't know about the latest updates to programming libraries. This knowledge gap exists because AI models have a "knowledge cutoff" – a point beyond which they haven't learned new information. Since software evolves rapidly, this limitation can lead to outdated recommendations and broken code.
Several innovative approaches have emerged to address this challenge:
llms.txt
A community-driven initiative where contributors create reference files (
llms.txt
) containing up-to-date library information specifically formatted for AI consumption.
Context7
A service that dynamically provides contextual information to AIs, often by intelligently summarizing documentation.
While these solutions are valuable, they face certain limitations:
llms.txt
files can become extraordinarily large – some exceeding
800,000
tokens (word fragments). This size can overwhelm many AI systems' context windows.
Many shorter
llms.txt
variants simply contain links to official documentation, requiring the AI to fetch and process those documents separately. Even the comprehensive versions (
llms-full.txt
) often exceed what most AI assistants can process at once. Additionally, these files may not always reflect the absolute latest documentation.
Context7
operates somewhat as a "black box" – while useful, its precise information selection methodology isn't fully transparent to users. It primarily works with GitHub code repositories or existing
llms.txt
files, rather than any arbitrary software package.
llm-min.txt
offers a fresh approach:
Inspired by
min.js
files in web development (JavaScript with unnecessary elements removed),
llm-min.txt
adopts a similar philosophy for technical documentation. Instead of feeding an AI a massive, verbose manual, we leverage another AI to distill that documentation into a super-condensed, highly structured summary. The resulting
llm-min.txt
file captures only the most essential information needed to understand a library's usage, packaged in a format optimized for AI assistants rather than human readers.
Modern AI reasoning capabilities excel at this distillation process, creating remarkably efficient knowledge representations that deliver maximum value with minimal token consumption.
Understanding
llm-min.txt
: A Machine-Optimized Format 🧩
The
llm-min.txt
file utilizes the
Structured Knowledge Format (SKF)
– a compact, machine-optimized format designed for efficient AI parsing rather than human readability. This format organizes technical information into distinct, highly structured sections with precise relationships.
Key Elements of the SKF Format:
Header Metadata:
Every file begins with essential contextual information:
# IntegratedKnowledgeManifest_SKF
: Format identifier and version
# SourceDocs: [...]
: Original documentation sources
# GenerationTimestamp: ...
: Creation timestamp
# PrimaryNamespace: ...
: Top-level package/namespace, critical for understanding import paths
Three Core Structured Sections:
The content is organized into distinct functional categories:
# SECTION: DEFINITIONS (Prefix: D)
: Describes the static aspects of the library:
Canonical component definitions with unique global IDs (e.g.,
D001:G001_MyClass
)
Namespace paths relative to
PrimaryNamespace
Method signatures with parameters and return types
Properties/fields with types and access modifiers
Static relationships like inheritance or interface implementation

data.title: How we made billing backendless
data.author: ayushrodrigues
data.article_summary: 文章介绍了Autumn团队尝试将支付和账单处理移到前端，以提供更好的开发者体验。最初，他们引入了一个"可发布密钥"（publishable key），让开发者可以直接在前端处理支付链接和检查功能访问权限，但发现该方案存在局限性和安全隐患。接着，他们尝试使用Next.js的服务器动作（server actions）来实现，但由于未认证的公共路由导致安全问题。最终，他们通过加密客户ID解决了部分安全问题，但意识到这种方法仅适用于支持服务器动作的框架。作者承认，未来可能放弃这种方法，转向更框架无关的方案，简化后端路由设置，使集成更加标准化和安全。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于“无后端计费”方案的可行性、安全性及其实际应用的讨论

不同观点：
• **Daviey**：认为“无后端计费”突显了开发体验（DX）与安全性之间的矛盾。虽然减少后端模板代码有吸引力，但安全性问题不可避免。特别是服务器操作中的IDOR漏洞（不安全的直接对象引用）是一个严重问题，仅靠前端无法解决。最终结论是，传统的“后端路由加认证”方法存在是有理由的。

• **biker142541**：对“无后端计费”的概念感到困惑，认为如果需要服务器操作，那就不是真正的无后端。建议更清晰地说明只是简化了后端交互，而不是完全去除后端。

• **taurath**：同样对文章感到不解，质疑为何计费需要webhooks和状态同步。认为可以在静态网站上接受支付而不需要webhooks，并提出这可能是在通过计费过程处理权限认证，而不是直接称之为认证。

• **beej71**：担心如果加密后的客户ID被获取，是否会导致客户被冒充。问题在于客户ID是否可被猜测，从而引发安全问题。

• **serbuvlad**：认为现代web技术越来越复杂且难以理解。强调任何支付处理都需要后端，所谓“无后端”只是混淆概念。同时也提到serverless实际上还是有服务器，只是形式不同。

• **singron**：提出服务器操作为何不能被认证，认为这是明显的解决方案。还提到密钥轮换和过期机制的问题，指出如果不解决这些问题，最终可能会重新发明类似JWT的机制。

• **robertlagrant**：建议直接对用户进行认证，然后可以安全地传递客户ID或使用替代键。提出可以使用JWT来实现这一点，特别是在无服务器函数中。

• **baobun**：认为团队正在重新发明JWT，建议深入了解JWT及其功能。

• **oulipo**：批评文章中的工程师缺乏基本的安全知识，指出多次事后才意识到方案不安全，令人担忧。

• **codegeek**：指出YC投资了类似的公司，useautumn与另一家YC公司getlago是直接竞争对手。

• **throwaway63467**：质疑服务器操作是否本身就是后端，认为如果需要服务器操作，那就不算是无后端。

• **delusional**：质疑在没有后端的情况下如何确保计费的准确性。提出用户可以通过控制台调用函数或修改代码，认为大多数多人在线游戏已经通过服务器权威模拟解决了类似问题。

补充讨论：
- 争议的焦点在于“无后端计费”是否可行及安全，特别是如何处理认证和授权问题。
- 多次提到JWT作为解决方案或类似概念，表明JWT在这种场景下的适用性和普遍性。
- 对“无后端”这一术语的混淆和质疑贯穿评论，反映出对新概念的理解和接受程度不一。
- 强调了安全性的重要性，尤其是在处理支付和客户数据时，不能仅依赖前端解决方案。

How we made billing backendless
Ayush, Autumn Co-Founder
We think handling payments on the frontend is a better developer experience.
Typically, billing is a backend job and requires webhooks, state syncing, then passing the data to the frontend. We wanted to offer a more "out-of-the-box" experience when handling things like payment links, paywalls and up/downgrade flows, and spent a bunch of time thinking about how we can perform sensitive operations without needing to perform the "round trip" to the backend.
This is a short write up of our exploration around the problem and why we ultimately are giving up.
Part 1: The Publishable Key
When we launched, we had a secret key that could be used securely from the backend just as Stripe does. Many of our first users had actually never set up Stripe before, and immediately told us they wish they could just do it from the frontend.
Our first solution was to create a "publishable key" which would let developers get payment links and check feature access (eg, does my user have any remaining credits) directly from the frontend, in an unprotected way. These functions alone can't really be abused.
The initial response was good and people were happy to use it with their initial set up. But we quickly ran into a couple problems:
It only worked with some endpoints (eg, tracking billable usage events had to be done via the secret key) and ended up confusing devs around which endpoints could be used with which keys.
Most software billing flows allow you to automatically purchase something if you've made a purchase before. This automatic purchasing (eg for upgrades) definitely couldn't be done with a public key.
Although it helped people spin up a sample integration fast, it quickly had to be ripped out anyway, so ended up being pretty pointless.
This still exists in our docs today and constantly trips people up. Can't wait to get rid of it.
Part 2: Server Actions
When we launched our Next.js library, we were excited to use server actions. The DX felt magical because users could:
Call them from the frontend like any normal function
The functions run on the server and can access our secret key stored as an ENV variable
No route set up needed, and the request is secure â nice!
Unfortunately we soon discovered our approach was flawed. Server actions are public, unauthenticated routes, and our API calls updates resources based on a
customer_id
field (eg. upgrade / downgrade requests, tracking usage for a feature, etc).
So if you got a hold of someone elseâs customer ID, you could make requests to the public server actions as if you were that customerâmaking this method insecure.
Part 3: Server actions + encryption
We really really liked the DX of server actions though, and so we had to brainstorm a way to overcome the customer ID being expoed in server action routes.
A few options came to mind, like using a middleware, or registering an authentication function, but the cleanest and simplest method we thought of was simply encrypting the customer ID:
Hereâs how it worked:
Our Provider was a server component, and so itâd take in a customer ID/user ID (server side), encrypt it using their API key, and pass it to context on the client side (see image below)
We wrap each server action with a client side function which grabs the
encryptedCustomerId
from context and passes it to the server action. These are all exported through a hook â
useAutumn
Each server action first decrypts the customer ID then calls the Autumn API
Essentially, we baked our own layer of auth into the server actions, and this is how our Next.js library works today. I haven't seen this approach by anyone else but essentially lets us fully handle secure payments, upgrades, downgrades, usage-based billing events â all from the frontend.
Weâre still not fully satisfied since this only works with frameworks that support server actions and SPA / vite is kinda making a comeback. It also makes the implementation different across frameworks.
The future
Ultimately I think we'll reach a point where we give up on this approach, and move towards a more framework agnostic approach. Rather than trying to abandon the backend route setup, we'll just make it easy to do. Take better-auth and how they generate their backend routes in just a couple lines of code â theyâve standardised the backend and frontend installation, and is pretty hard to get wrong.
Other companies like Polar have a similar approach and are heavily praised for it. We probably don't need to reinvent the wheel (as fun as it is).
The easiest way to integrate Stripe âº

• **oulipo**：批评文章中的工程师缺乏基本的安全知识，指出多次事后才意识到方案不安全，令人担忧。

- 多次提到JWT作为解决方案或类似概念，表明JWT在这种场景下的适用性和普遍性。

data.article_summary: 2011年，拉里·佩奇（Larry Page）成为谷歌CEO后，试图通过缩减项目和改革会议制度来提升公司效率。他规定会议必须有决策者、参会人数不得超过10人、每位参会者需有贡献，且会议应为50分钟以留出休息时间。然而，谷歌日历团队将默认会议时长改为25和50分钟后，效果不如预期。许多人仍按习惯将会议拖到整点，导致50分钟后的10分钟空档被其他团队利用。一个纽约办公室的团队利用这些空档安排自己的站立会议，严格遵守规则并“恶意合规”地抢占会议室，引发了一些混乱和不满。最终，改革未带来实质性变化。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于会议时间安排和规则执行的讨论，包括对所谓“恶意合规”（malicious compliance）的定义和实际操作的争议。

不同观点：
• **关于“恶意合规”的定义**：
  - [remram] 和 [dcre] 认为这不是“恶意合规”，而是“迂腐执行”（pedantic enforcement）或“混乱中立执行”（chaotic neutral compliance）。真正的“恶意合规”应涉及故意利用规则来制造麻烦，例如预订连续的会议。
  - [nyrikki] 则提出自己曾通过加入不必要的长时间会议来获得空闲时间，认为这可以视为一种“恶意合规”。

• **会议时间管理和执行的有效性**：
  - [drewg123] 和 [gwbas1c] 支持通过外部限制（如会议室预订）来强制结束会议，认为这有助于避免会议拖延。
  - [exhilaration] 提出可以通过调整会议开始时间（如9:10开始）来自然形成结束点，而不是硬性规定会议时长。
  - [grimpy] 分享了在Google时领导试图通过规定“会议间5分钟间隔”来提高效率，但最终导致混乱的经历。

• **规则执行和遵守的必要性**：
  - [Artoooooor] 强调规则应被遵守，如果规则长期未被执行，应该修改或加强执行，而不是将其视为一纸空文。
  - [palmotea] 认为某些领导在制定规则时未考虑实际情况，导致不切实际的规则执行。

• **会议形式和必要性的讨论**：
  - [lesser23] 提出短会议（如站会）应通过在线工具（如Slack）进行，以避免浪费时间，并指出两种常见问题：领导浪费时间的讨论和工程师间的细争论。
  - [xivzgrev] 质疑是否所有会议（特别是站会）都需要会议室，认为规则应根据实际需求灵活调整。

• **文化背景和幽默案例**：
  - [isaacimagine] 提到MIT的讲座时间安排（MIT时间），所有讲座开始和结束都有5分钟缓冲，以此为例说明规则的灵活性。
  - [havblue] 分享了DefCon视频中的幽默案例，讲者拒绝提前结束演讲，强调这是他们的时间，反映了规则执行中的对抗。

补充讨论：
- [flerchin] 提到站会（standup）通常是站着快速进行的，因此不一定需要会议室，呼应了关于会议形式和规则的讨论。
- 总体上，讨论反映了不同组织在会议管理和规则执行中的多样实践和挑战，以及员工如何应对不合理或不切实际的规定。

Malicious compliance by booking an available meeting room
In 2011, Larry Page became CEO of Google and tried to fix meetings. But his new policies were no match for Google Calendar pedants.
Jacob Voytko
May 15, 2025
1
Share this post

1
Share
Back in 2011, Larry Page became the CEO of Google in place of Eric Schmidt. This happened at a time when Google was feeling the growing pains of becoming a huge company. It had 30,000 employees and was growing rapidly. But you could really feel the weight; projects were getting more ambitious, taking longer, and often failing more spectacularly.
At the time, I remember an anecdote told by Larry Page. He said that companies like Yahoo! used to be a punchline at Google because it would take them weeks to get something onto their homepage. Google could accomplish the same thing in a few hours, or a few days at worst. But now he was the CEO of a company where it took weeks to get something onto the homepage, and he was sure that he was the butt of some startup’s jokes.
Thanks for reading Client/Server! Subscribe for free to receive new posts and support my work.
Subscribe
Anyways, all of this clearly bothered Larry Page. He wanted to fix it. One of his first actions was to shutter tons of projects that didn’t make tactical or strategic sense, and focus on fewer efforts. This came with the catch phrase “more wood behind fewer arrows.” For example, they shuttered
Google Buzz
so that it wouldn’t distract from
Google+
.
And second, Larry Page emailed the whole company
a ham-fisted attempt to revamp how meetings were done
.
Every meeting needed a “decision-maker.”
Meetings should be capped at 10 people.
Everybody in a meeting should give input or they shouldn’t be in the meeting.
Hour-long meetings should be only 50 minutes to give the participants an opportunity to use the restroom between meetings.
They later softened some of the language by saying that these were properties of “decision-oriented meetings,” implying there were other types of meetings that someone might need to attend. But you could never shake the feeling that Larry Page had to make decisions all day long and forgot that sometimes people meet for other reasons.
Anyways, let’s focus on the fact that Larry Page wanted hour-long meetings to only be 50 minutes. This is a good thing! It gives people a chance to stretch, go to the bathroom, grab a snack, etc. During a Q/A on the changes
1
, someone asked him whether Google Calendar should default to 25 and 50 minutes for meeting lengths instead of 30 and 60 minutes. Larry Page said “yes.” And then someone on the Google Calendar team implemented this.
And then nothing changed. When 2:50 rolled around and your meeting was supposed to end, do you think people actually ended the meeting? Noooooo. Absolutely not! Meetings continue until the participants of the next meeting are clawing on your door like a pack of zombies.
At one point, one team in the NYC office noticed that their standups were about 10 minutes long. They didn’t want to compete with meetings that respected the half-hour boundaries. And why would they need to? Every meeting room had free slots at the last 10 minutes of every hour because people were now booking 50-minute meetings. So they did what any rational engineering team would do: they started booking their standup in the tiny 10-minute time slices that were free on the calendar of every meeting room.
I found this out when I saw them knock on the door to a meeting room by my desk. 2:50 rolls around and someone knocks on the door and says “I have the meeting room.”
The person in the room responds, “No you don’t, it’s 2:50.”
“Look again at the room’s calendar. You booked a 50-minute meeting, we have the room for the last 10 minutes of the hour for our standup.”
I could hear the muffled exasperation. “You’ve got to be joking me.”
“We have the room, sorry.”
Then everyone shuffled out of the room, looking vaguely pissed off. And who could blame them! Can you imagine if someone actually held you to this policy? You’re there stammering “it’s the default, I meant for the room to be ours for an hour” and they counter with the fact that their names are listed as the active participant? I mean, I’d personally tell them that I wasn’t going to leave the room, but surely it worked a lot?
I wish I knew the identities of these brave meeting crashers. I saw them pull this stunt twice and then ride off into the sunset, and I never got to learn what team they were on. I wish I knew their motivations. Were they true believers in the 50-minute policy? Were they bored pedants? Were they wraiths, cursed to hunt the office for available meeting rooms? I’ll never know for sure.
1
Likely at a TGIF, but truthfully I don’t remember.

data.title: Lua for Elixir
data.author: davydog187
data.article_summary:
2025年5月12日，Elixir库Lua发布了首个稳定版本v0.1.0，该库允许在BEAM VM上直接执行隔离的Lua程序，完全实现了Lua 5.3，而无需嵌入C语言的Lua运行时和编译器。这是通过Luerl库实现的，Luerl是用Erlang实现的Lua解析器、编译器和运行时。Lua Elixir库扩展了Luerl的功能，改进了错误信息并提供了详细的文档。主要功能包括通过`deflua`宏将Elixir API暴露给Lua，使用`~LUA`符号在编译时验证Lua语法，以及提供详细的文档和Livebook示例。

该库起源于TV Labs，用于执行任意代码以进行高层次的集成测试。未来计划包括改进Luerl的错误消息、文档和与Lua生态的深度集成，并计划合并Elixir Lua库到Luerl，发布2.0.0版本。感兴趣的开发者可以通过Slack、Discord参与或在Github上提交问题。

43972485.article_content:
Published
May 12, 2025
Introducing Lua for Elixir
The first stable release of the Elixir library,
Lua v0.1.0
, has been released to
hex.pm
!
Lua is a library that allows you to execute arbitrary, sandboxed
Lua
programs directly on the BEAM VM. This is
not
embedding the C Lua runtime and compiler, but rather a complete implementation of Lua 5.3. This feat is made possible by the underlying
Luerl library
, which implements a Lua parser, compiler, and runtime, all in Erlang.
The Lua Elixir library extends the capabilities of the Luerl library, improving error messages and providing robust documentation.
Feature highlights include:
Extending Lua with Elixir APIs
The Lua Elixir library has a
deflua
macro for easily expressing APIs in Elixir that can be exposed to Lua with
Lua.load_api/2
defmodule MyAPI do
use Lua.API
deflua double(v), do: 2 * v
end
import Lua, only: [sigil_LUA: 2]
lua = Lua.new() |> Lua.load_api(MyAPI)
{[10], _} = Lua.eval!(lua, ~LUA[return double(5)])
Compile-time syntax evaluation
A
~LUA
sigil is exposed, allowing the validation of Lua syntax at Elixir compile time.
iex> import Lua, only: [sigil_LUA: 2]
#iex> {[4], _} = Lua.eval!(~LUA[return 2 +])
** (Lua.CompilerException) Failed to compile Lua!
Robust documentation
See the
Lua Hex docs
for detailed documentation and examples for working with Lua and Luerl.
A
Livebook
is also available to get you started.
Born at TV Labs
The Lua Elixir library started as a proof of concept at
TV Labs
, where I am co-founder and CTO. At TV Labs, we needed to execute arbitrary code to allow our customers to write high-level integration tests against physical televisions and other streaming media devices. What started as a prototype led to diving deep into the particulars of Luerl, improving its usability and error messages, while making it easy to use from Elixir. TV Labs uses Lua as a compilation target for its
drag and drop Automation builder
, where users can specify the high-level workflow of their tests, and we handle the scheduling and underlying execution.
The Elixir Lua library and Luerl have allowed us to build a working solution for vision-based integration tests on physical devices, without needing to orchestrate additional Javascript or Python virtual machines, and executing the code on compute right next to the physical device.
How Luerl came to be
Robert Virding is a living legend. Beyond being a
famous movie star
, Robert is best known for collaborating with
Joe Armstrong
and Mike Williams at Ericsson in the mid-80s to create the
Erlang Programming Language
. Erlang is originally known for its use in telecommunications and its properties of fault-tolerance, concurrency, and immutable data, but is now regarded as a general purpose language, with its virtual machine, the BEAM VM, powering many languages including Elixir and Gleam. Since it wasn’t fun to just create
one
programming language, Robert also created
Lisp flavored Erlang (LFE)
, a Prolog interpreter in Erlang called
Erlog
, and of course, an implementation of Lua called
Luerl
.
During
Code BEAM EU 2024
, I had the honor of
giving a talk
with Robert. Since Luerl seemed to be a side project for him, I asked him why he bothered creating it in the first place. Robert smirked and said:
I wrote a Prolog on Erlang, that was fun. Then I wrote a functional Lisp in Erlang, that was fun too. But then I realized that it would be neat to implement an imperative or object-oriented language on the BEAM, so I picked Lua and had at it. That’s how Luerl was born.
If I’ve learned anything from this experience and collaborating with Robert, it’s that he still gets immense joy from creating and experimenting, and Luerl is one of those many examples.
The future of Lua and Luerl
Lua has been a great foundation for building our automation platform at TV Labs; however, there are many improvements needed in Luerl to make it more useful:
The quality of error messages needs to be dramatically improved
Stacktraces often lack useful context and information
Documentation and examples need significant work
Sandboxing features related to memory need more examination and exploration
Deeper integration with the larger Lua ecosystem
To that end, Robert and I have discussed merging the Elixir Lua library into Luerl. We hope to do this and release a 2.0.0 version of Luerl, continuing to improve documentation, remove deprecated interfaces, and dramatically improve error messages and stack traces.
If you’re interested in getting involved, join the
Slack
or
Discord
, or
open an issue on Github
.
Thanks!

data.article_summary:
这篇文章介绍了如何在Rust中实现类似于Python的动态API，特别是利用`serde`库来模拟Python的`__getattr__`功能。作者希望在Rust中创建一个用户友好的API，类似于Python中通过WMI包获取系统信息的简便方法。文章首先展示了Python中通过动态属性访问系统信息的代码，然后说明了如何在Rust中实现等效的“原始”API，但这种原始API使用起来较为繁琐，需要手动检查和处理各种数据类型。

为了改善用户体验，作者提出了一种受Python启发的设计，允许用户定义自定义结构体（如`Fan`），并通过泛型函数`query`返回这些结构体的实例。文章最后讨论了如何通过定义新trait来实现这一功能，使API更直观易用。这一设计的核心在于利用Rust的泛型和trait功能来实现类似于Python的动态行为。

43954858.article_content:
A Rust API Inspired by Python, Powered by Serde
May 7, 2025
rust
python
api
design
Years ago, I worked on reimplementing
1
some Python code in Rust (
yet again
),
and this time I needed to adapt Python’s dynamic capabilities (aka
__getattr__
) to the strict and compiled world of Rust.
After some deliberation, and armed with the
serde
(de)serialization crate, I set out to do just that.
So if you ever wondered what tricks Rust can learn from Python, and if
serde
can be used for reflection (please go along with me here), then the answer is very much yes!
Let me show you how, and also why.
Note: I’ll try to keep this somewhat approachable to Python programmers with only passing experience in Rust, it’ll be fun.
🦀🐍
A Python Inspiration
Using Python (on Windows), there’s a
magical package
that can be used to get all sorts of information about the system.
Without going into too much detail, it boils down to this: Say you want to list all the installed
physical fans
. You can do that using the following code:
import
wmi
c
=
wmi
.
WMI
()
for
fan
in
c
.
Win32_Fan
():
if
fan
.
ActiveCooling
:
print
(
f
"Fan `
{
fan
.
Name
}
` is running at
{
fan
.
DesiredSpeed
}
RPM"
)
This uses a couple of clever
__getattr__
implementations, and ends up running this equivalent code behind the scenes:
for
fan
in
c
.
query
(
"SELECT * FROM Win32_Fan"
):
if
fan
.
wmi_property
(
"ActiveCooling"
)
.
value
is
True
:
print
(
f
"Fan `
{
fan
.
wmi_property
(
'Name'
)
.
value
}
` is running at
{
fan
.
wmi_property
(
'DesiredSpeed'
)
.
value
}
RPM"
)
(The
wmi_property
method returns another object which holds the final value as well as its type.)
Putting aside
what
WMI
even is
, this is the kind of thing Python is extraordinarily good at:
A clear, concise, and intuitive interface abstracting over a complex and gnarly implementation.
In Python, you need but override a few magic methods to implement this, but Rust is a completely different beast.
What can we do if we want to create a Rust crate that provides a nice API to users, similar to the one above?
What We Are Abstracting Over
It’ll help to start by expressing the “raw” API in pure Rust. It’s raw in the sense that we can use it to get the
raw data
from the system, but nothing more.
We have two types: the
Value
type that can hold different types of values,
and the
Object
type that provides access to named attributes (which are themselves
Value
instances).
We end up with something like this (the full code is available
on GitHub
):
mod
raw_api
{
pub
struct
Object
{
..
}
pub
enum
Value
{
Bool
(
bool
),
I1
(
i8
),
// ..
UI8
(
u64
),
String
(
String
),
Object
(
Object
),
}
impl
Object
{
pub
fn
get_attr
(
&
self
,
name:
&
str
)
->
Value
{
..
}
}
pub
fn
query
(
query:
&
str
)
->
Vec
<
Object
>
{
..
}
}
Simple, but rather painful for the user to work with:
let
res
=
raw_api::query
(
"SELECT * FROM Win32_Fan"
);
for
obj
in
res
{
if
obj
.
get_attr
(
"ActiveCooling"
)
==
Value::Bool
(
true
)
{
if
let
Value::
String
(
name
)
=
obj
.
get_attr
(
"Name"
)
{
if
let
Value::
UI8
(
speed
)
=
obj
.
get_attr
(
"DesiredSpeed"
)
{
println!
(
"Fan `
{name}
` is running at
{speed}
RPM"
);
}
}
}
}
Since any field can be of any type, the user must manually check (either with
match
or, as we did, with
if let
)
what variant of the
Value
enum they got every time they interact with it.
This is especially cumbersome when one wants to query many different types of objects (
Win32_Battery
🔋,
Win32_UserAccount
💁,
Win32_Printer
🖨️, …).
Note: this is a simplification of the
underlying API
we have to use,
but it’s close enough that we can design our higher level API based on it. You can check the
wmi-rs
crate
source code for the full details.
A Possible Design
Inspired by the Pythonic API, what if instead we could do something like this:
// 1. The user defines a custom struct for the type of objects to query.
struct
Fan
{
name:
String
,
active_cooling:
bool
,
desired_speed:
u64
,
}
// 2. Specify that `query` should to return instances of `Fan`.
let
res:
Vec
<
Fan
>
=
api::query
();
// 3. Profit.
for
fan
in
res
{
if
fan
.
active_cooling
{
println!
(
"Fan `
{}
` is running at
{}
RPM"
,
fan
.
name
,
fan
.
desired_speed
);
}
}
Much nicer!
One of the distinct features of Rust is that
generic return types
can change the behavior of a function
(with
.collect()
being the most famous example of this), so how can we implement something like this?
Imagine we went ahead and updated
query
to accept some generic type
T
.
What trait can we use to constrain
T
so we can implement the function?
fn
query
<
T
>
()
->
Vec
<
T
>
where
T:
???
{
???
}
The standard library offers
any::type_name
which could (not really) help us to build the
SELECT
query,
but without resorting to
violence
, we seem to be on our own.
Crawl Before You Can Walk
Let’s start with a relatively simple solution: Let’s
define a new trait
that:
Provides the name of the object to query.
Handles the construction of e.g.
Fan
s from
Object
s.
This will give us a firm ground to stand on

data.title: Pathfinding
data.author: sebg
data.article_summary: JuhrJuhr在其游戏开发日志中介绍了NPC路径寻找的实现方法，特别强调了适应动态物理环境、保持与障碍物的距离、以及游戏区域边界环绕等独特需求。为了处理动态环境，他采用A*搜索算法，结合空间分区树来减少每次路径查询的计算量。空间分区树将游戏区域划分为不同层次的节点，通过缓存和定期刷新（每500毫秒）来保持路径的实时更新。路径选择上，算法优先选择离障碍物较远但必要时可以靠近的路线，并支持类似《Asteroids》游戏的边界环绕效果。这种方法有效平衡了路径搜索的效率和自然性。

Hello!
I've recently been working on the pathfinding for NPCs in my game, which is something I've been looking forward to for a while now since it's a nice chunky problem to solve. I thought I'd write up this post about how I went about it all.
I had a few extra requirements of my pathfinding, due to how my game plays:
Must deal with a dynamic physical environment (objects can move freely and are destructible)
Have paths that prefer to keep their distance from objects but still get close when needed
Allow for wrapping around the borders of the game area (Asteroids style)
General Approach
My first thought was that I wanted detailed paths so that they could thread through messy arrangements of objects quite easily. This would mean a longer search time, so the simple choice of search algorithm is A*. And since I need to query the world for each node to see whether it's blocked, I thought I'd use space partitioning with the queries to cut down on the number required for each path.
I ended up sticking to this plan, and figuring out the more detailed stuff along the way.
Space Partitioned Queries
I built a space partitioning tree where each node covers a specific area of the game, and then each of that node's children covers a specific area of their parent's area (with the tree's root covering the whole game area). I do this to a depth of 6 and then the leaf nodes effectively make up the navigation grid for path finding.
Now when I check if a node is blocked it will first check its parent. If its parent is not blocked, then none of its children are blocked. If the parent is blocked, then the child node needs to run its own query to see whether its own area is blocked. This allows us to know whether large areas of the game are not blocked in very few queries, which is useful because these queries are expensive.
A* Search
The actual search is a pretty standard A* search. Each node has 8 neighbours, with nodes on the edge having wrapped neighbours, which are cached along with their traversal cost for faster lookup.
Environment Changing in Real Time
Because objects can move around in the game world and even have chunks of them destroyed, this algorithm needed to be able to update in real time. The asteroid that wasn't blocking the path a second ago might have moved, and the asteroid that was blocking the path might have been blown up!
My simple solution for this was to allow the algorithm to cache whether each node it checked was blocked, but then invalidate that cache every so often (currently every 500ms is working nicely). This allows time to build up a picture of the world and let one path finding request use information from a previous request, but also forces the algorithm to keep up to date on the current state of the world.
Ideally we wouldn't invalidate the whole cache since there will be sections of the game world where nothing has moved, but realistically this is a simple approach that works well enough. Saying that, I do have a plan on how to do this should it be necessary.
Here you can see the spreading out and being updated in real time. Each blue square represents an unblocked node, and the colour of the pixel in the node represents proximity to the nearest object.
Natural Paths
The shortest path doesn't usually look natural, or safe for that matter, so I wanted the algorithm to prefer paths that are further away from objects but still be able to get close when necessary (threading through a small gap, for example).
So for each pathfinding request a preferred distance from objects is provided, which is then used to give each node a proximity rating. This proximity rating is used when determining the traversal cost to a node, so nodes that are closer to objects are simply more expensive when running the search.
Currently the proximity rating has an exponential effect, so the path really tries to avoid being super close to things, but doesn't mind being a little close if it has to.
Here you can see the path keeping its distance from objects until its forced to get closer and in between them. You can also see the space partitioning better here, with the larger blue squares representing areas that only required a single query.
Wrapped Paths
Because the game area allows for Asteroids-like wrapping, I wanted the pathfinding to account for this too. NPCs not having the same kind of mobility as the player is a bit jarring, plus it made the problem a little more fun to solve. :)
Wrapped paths mean that every navigation node actually has the same number of neighbours, which is an interesting and maybe uncommon property (pathfinding on a 3d globe probably has the same property).

43994333.article_summary: JuhrJuhr在其游戏开发日志中介绍了NPC路径寻找的实现方法，特别强调了适应动态物理环境、保持与障碍物的距离、以及游戏区域边界环绕等独特需求。为了处理动态环境，他采用A*搜索算法，结合空间分区树来减少每次路径查询的计算量。空间分区树将游戏区域划分为不同层次的节点，通过缓存和定期刷新（每500毫秒）来保持路径的实时更新。路径选择上，算法优先选择离障碍物较远但必要时可以靠近的路线，并支持类似《Asteroids》游戏的边界环绕效果。这种方法有效平衡了路径搜索的效率和自然性。

data.title: My Engineering Craft Regressed
data.author: OsrsNeedsf2P
data.article_summary: 本文作者讲述了自己大学毕业后，投身开源项目并获得用户认可，但在求职过程中发现招聘方并不重视这些实际项目。在申请600多份工作后，仅获得3个offer，最终选择了一家待遇一般但尊重他的公司。之后，作者继续在开源项目上投入大量时间，但这些努力并未带来预期的高薪工作。为了提高收入，作者开始专注于Leetcode刷题，最终获得了5倍薪资增长，尽管技能有所退步，却受到多家公司青睐。作者对开源世界的热情逐渐冷却，计划赚够钱后退休，希望那时的开源社区仍保持原样。
data.comments_summary:

不同观点：
• picafrost认为，项目本身并不能全面反映候选人的团队合作能力和稳定性。他更关注候选人是否能持续参与团队活动，并信任一个稳定的开发人员，而不是一个可能给团队带来麻烦的“明星”开发者。

• ZephyrBlu指出，技能和市场需求之间的不对等现象。即使技能退步，一些人仍因其名声而更受欢迎，这种现象让人感觉荒谬。

5 years ago when I graduated University, I had a whole host of open source projects under my belt. I put my heart and soul into them - for thousands of hours. And users loved them. I still remember some of the faceless users whose messages gave me a smile.
When I went into the job market - which was much better back then - I had some incorrect assumption that recruiters would care about this work. Or at least technically inclined companies. Or at the very least, companies
I
would want to work for would care about this.
But that never happened. My Indeed profile shows I applied to over 600 jobs back then. With 3 offers, I accepted the only one that didn’t treat me like a baby, and had a great time working for that company.
During the day, I worked 8-9 hours for this startup, and until late at night I continued my open source contributions. Surely, they would take me somewhere.
I hopped to another startup and oversaw major projects - for pitiful pay - but enjoyed it. My skillset had never been so strong, and my impact was measurably through the roof. Surely if I kept this up, I would land a high paying gig anytime soon.
But of course, that didn’t happen. Waking up at 6am to make some commits, reading documentation on the subway, and coding to dubstep at night wasn’t getting me anywhere. But I was happy.
Eventually I came to face the music - Nobody gives a crap about real projects. The people who knew my value weren’t the people who could pay me. I peeled back, and started grinding Leetcode instead.
My projects slowed to a crawl. The communities slowly got demotivated. It was sad to turn my back to, but it got me a 5x salary bump.
When I joined, I was treated like a baby for having “4 years of industry experience”. Whatever. I did work here and there, and apparently my impact exceeded expectations.
But what about my skillset? Despite significantly regressing, now my email is filled with recruiters begging me to come to be “Amazon SDE II”, “Tech lead at YC startup X”, “Part time job paying 150-290$/hr”. Pathetic. I was so much better (and happier) before, yet I’m only seen when I do the fake crap like update my LinkedIn to celebrate 1 year at $FAANG.
I’ll collect some money and retire in a couple years. Hopefully the open source world stays the same until then.

data.title: California sent residents' personal health data to LinkedIn
data.author: anticorporate
data.article_summary: 《The Markup》调查发现，加州平价医疗法案（Affordable Care Act）的健康保险网站coveredca.com向LinkedIn传输敏感数据。当用户填写有关是否失明、怀孕、使用多种处方药等问题时，网站上的跟踪器会将这些信息发送给LinkedIn，甚至包括是否为跨性别者或家暴受害者。该行为是在一个广告活动中进行的，目前这些跟踪器已被移除。Covered California表示正在审查数据安全和隐私协议，确保不会非法共享用户信息。此事件引发了对隐私违规的担忧，有专家指出这种做法侵犯了用户隐私。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Covered California向LinkedIn等平台泄露敏感健康信息的问题，以及相关数据追踪和隐私保护的争议。

不同观点：
• [kordlessagain] 认为，Covered California泄露敏感健康信息的问题反映了更广泛的行业问题，即原本用于护理的基础设施被用于广告行为 targeting。作者质疑科技公司和AI系统背后的动机，认为这些行为并非出于智慧，而是出于权力集中和恐惧落后。
• [vharuck] 认为，Covered California使用60多个追踪器是故意为之，而非简单的失误。他对为什么一个仅处理健康保险的独立机构需要如此多的追踪器表示疑惑，并指出这种行为明显不妥。
• [bensonn] 强调，称这些数据为“泄露”并不准确，因为添加LinkedIn追踪代码是故意行为，追踪器按设计执行了其功能。他指出，这是Covered California的选择，而非意外。
• [neilv] 分享了个人经历，LinkedIn根据其浏览历史展示了相关广告，质疑是否有人将私人医疗信息提供给了LinkedIn。
• [oaththrowaway] 质疑为什么一个州级机构需要进行广告追踪，认为这可能是为了资金需求。
• [1024core] 直接指出这种行为可能违反HIPAA法案，并对此表示惊讶。
• [knowitnone] 认为，加州的调查可能会偏袒自己，且指出LinkedIn与Microsoft的关系。
• [blindriver] 询问定期清除cookies是否能防止长期追踪。
• [goldchainposse] 解释说，许多公司主动将数据提供给大科技公司，而非出售数据，科技公司利用这些数据进行广告投放。

The website that lets Californians shop for health insurance under the Affordable Care Act, coveredca.com, has been sending sensitive data to  LinkedIn, forensic testing by The Markup has revealed.
As visitors filled out forms on the website, trackers on the same pages told LinkedIn their answers to questions about whether they were blind, pregnant, or used a high number of prescription medications. The trackers also monitored whether the visitors said they were transgender or possible victims of domestic abuse.
See our data here
Github
Covered California, the organization that operates the website, removed the trackers as The Markup and CalMatters reported this article. The organization said they were removed “due to a marketing agency transition” in early April.
In a statement, Kelly Donohue, a spokesperson for the agency, confirmed that data was sent to LinkedIn as part of an advertising campaign. Since  being informed of the tracking, “all active advertising-related tags across our website have been turned off out of an abundance of caution,” she added.
“Covered California has initiated a review of our websites and information security and privacy protocols to ensure that no analytics tools are impermissibly sharing sensitive consumer information,” Donohue said, adding that they would “share additional findings as they become available, taking any necessary steps to safeguard the security and privacy of consumer data.”
When an individual indicated they were pregnant, the information was sent to LinkedIn via the Insight Tag.
Credit:
Visitors who filled out health information on the site may have had their data tracked for more than a year, according to Donohue, who said the LinkedIn campaign began in February 2024.

data.author: _kush
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：HDR技术在游戏、摄影和显示器中的应用及其优缺点

不同观点：
• Terr_认为，人眼的自然视觉可以动态调整光照和焦距，而目前的游戏中HDR和景深效果往往降低体验的真实感，导致颜色和模糊问题，直到 gaze-tracking 技术普及才能解决。
• Asafira 提供了有关HDR的科普资源，并通过自身的专业背景（AMO物理学）说明了HDR在相机技术中的应用，强调了HDR技术在摄影中的实际价值。
• Dahart 指出，HDR捕捉、格式和工作流与HDR显示是不同的概念，并澄清Ansel Adams并没有使用现代意义上的HDR技术，混淆这些概念只会引起更多困惑。
• CarVac 表示，HDR显示在高亮部分（如白色墙壁）的处理上让人不适，并且在色调映射上倾向于低对比度，不符合个人口味。
• Caseyy 通过幽默的方式表达了对HDR在影视中应用的看法，特别是夜晚观看影片时HDR效果带来的不适。
• Gyomu 作为摄影师，指出HDR内容在实际显示中存在亮度不一致的问题，尤其是在夜间使用低亮度浏览内容时更为明显。
• Aidenn0 提到HDR技术的普及面临基础设施升级的巨大成本问题，消费者对HDR显示的接受度也受到设备更换周期的影响。
• Gwbas1c 强调计算机无法读取人类意图，因此在软件开发中理解这一点很重要，间接提到HDR内容生成中AI的局限性。
• Sergioisidoro 补充了模拟摄影中通过开发者控制动态范围的方法，并批评手机HDR照片在创意摄影中的表现。
• The__alchemist 对HDR显示器的实用性表示好奇，并提到HDR在真实场景与照片显示之间的差距。
• Echo_time 提到在不同浏览器（Firefox和Chrome）中查看HDR相关内容时的体验差异，可能与浏览器设置有关。
• Chaboud 详细说明了HDR在专业视频/电影工具中的演变，强调了色彩和亮度描述的绝对意义，并介绍了相关技术标准。
• Mxfh 对某些文章中HDR解释的不满，认为文章没有解决消费者数字环境中的色彩管理问题，并指出HDR UI设计中的亮度问题。
• Kristianp 提供了一个关于Sigma相机HDR功能的文章链接，展示了较为成功的HDR照片案例。
• Hfgjbcgjbvg 简单表达了对数字相机技术的兴趣。

补充讨论：
• HDR技术的定义和应用范围存在混淆，特别是在摄影和显示领域，不同观点对HDR的实际效果和使用体验存在分歧。
• 浏览器兼容性和HDR内容显示问题也被提及，表明在网络环境中HDR技术的实现仍存在挑战。
• 讨论中多次提到HDR技术的实际体验问题，包括高亮部分处理不当、UI设计中的亮度问题等，表明HDR技术在消费级应用中仍需改进。
• 对HDR技术普及的成本和消费者接受度的讨论，反映了技术从专业领域向消费领域普及的现实障碍。

data.title: Forget IPs: using cryptography to verify bot and agent traffic
data.author: todsacerdoti
data.article_summary:
本文讨论了在AI代理流量增加的背景下，如何区分合法爬虫和恶意机器人。传统上，Cloudflare依靠用户代理头和IP地址验证爬虫身份，但这些方法存在易被伪造和不准确的问题。为了解决这一问题，文章提出了两种新的认证机制——HTTP消息签名和请求mTLS，以帮助友好机器人验证自身身份。

现有方法的问题包括：用户代理头易被伪造，IP地址共享和变化频繁，以及每个网站单独共享秘密（如Bearer token）不切实际。新机制利用加密技术，使机器人开发者能够对其服务发出的请求进行加密签名，从而使像Cloudflare这样的反向代理能够验证请求来源，帮助网站所有者更好地管理流量。

HTTP消息签名是一种标准化的请求加密认证方式，使来源能够确认发送者身份。请求mTLS则通过双向TLS验证实现更强的安全性。文章还邀请开发者参与其封闭测试。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：如何应对恶意流量和爬虫活动，以及在技术上可能的解决方案和隐私问题。

不同观点：
• Lockhead认为，虽然该方法可以帮助检测合法的机器人，但仍然难以区分真实用户和恶意流量。合法的机器人数量较少且行为透明，容易识别，但要实现该方法的实际应用，用户需要参与，这会引发隐私问题。

• Ok123456建议在SMTP中引入工作量证明扩展，使得小型SMTP中继可以通过解决计算问题来增加邮件投递的机会，且问题的难度可以与发送者的声誉成反比。

• Unsolved73对当前使用 obscure RFC 而非更普遍的 JSON Web Tokens（JWTs）的HTTP签名方法提出质疑，认为这可能导致有趣的漏洞。

• PaulHoule指出，AI训练和推理都是驱动机器人活动的重要因素。尤其是AI推理可以通过自动生成爬虫代码和执行复杂的工作流来增加爬虫的使用，但这些活动可能因验证码等问题而中断。

• Nubinetwork反对对HTTP请求进行复杂分析，认为这会增加服务器负担，不利于运行网站。

• Dboreham猜测，这种技术讨论的潜台词可能是为爬虫流量引入收费。

• Senectus1分享了一个自托管的类似解决方案，并对其表示赞赏。

• Superkuh批评依赖中心化的证书机构和短寿命密钥的技术方案，认为这会提高人类参与网络的难度，最终可能导致网络的封闭化。

补充讨论：
- 争议焦点在于技术实现的复杂性、隐私问题以及对用户和开发者的影响。
- 讨论中涉及的具体技术包括工作量证明、HTTP签名、SMTP扩展、自托管解决方案等。
- 部分评论者关注爬虫活动对网络资源的消耗，以及如何有效限制恶意流量而不影响合法机器人。
- 另一个值得注意的方面是对网络基础设施集中化的担忧，以及对未来网络开放性的潜在影响。

43994779.article_content:
Forget IPs: using cryptography to verify bot and agent traffic
2025-05-15
Thibault Meunier
Mari Galicer
10 min read
With the rise of traffic from AI agents, whatâs considered a bot is no longer clear-cut. There are some clearly malicious bots, like ones that DoS your site or do credential stuffing, and ones that most site owners do want to interact with their site, like the bot that indexes your site for a search engine, or ones that fetch RSS feeds.Â Â Â Â Â Â
Historically, Cloudflare has relied on two main signals to verify legitimate web crawlers from other types of automated traffic: user agent headers and IP addresses. The
User-Agent
header
allows bot developers to identify themselves, i.e.
MyBotCrawler/1.1
. However, user agent headers alone are easily spoofed and are therefore insufficient for reliable identification. To address this, user agent checks are often supplemented with
IP address validation
, the inspection of published IP address ranges to confirm a crawler's authenticity. However, the logic around IP address ranges representing a product or group of users is brittle â connections from the crawling service might be shared by multiple users, such as in the case of
privacy proxies
and VPNs, and these ranges, often maintained by cloud providers, change over time.
Cloudflare will always try to block malicious bots, but we think our role here is to also provide an affirmative mechanism to authenticate desirable bot traffic. By using well-established cryptography techniques, weâre proposing a better mechanism for legitimate agents and bots to declare who they are, and provide a clearer signal for site owners to decide what traffic to permit.Â
Today, weâre introducing two proposals â HTTP message signatures and request mTLS â for
friendly bots
to authenticate themselves, and for customer origins to identify them.
In this blog post, weâll share how these authentication mechanisms work, how we implemented them, and how you can participate in our closed beta.
Existing bot verification mechanisms are brokenÂ
Historically, if youâve worked on ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, or any other agent, youâve had several options to identify your HTTP traffic to other services:Â
You define a
user agent
, an HTTP header described in
RFC 9110
. The problem here is that this header is easily spoofable and thereâs not a clear way for agents to identify themselves as semi-automated browsers â agents often use the Chrome user agent for this very reason, which is discouraged. The RFC
states
:
âIf a user agent masquerades as a different user agent, recipients can assume that the user intentionally desires to see responses tailored for that identified user agent, even if they might not work as well for the actual user agent being used.â
Â
You publish your IP address range(s). This has limitations because the same IP address might be shared by multiple users or multiple services within the same company, or even by multiple companies when hosting infrastructure is shared (like Cloudflare Workers, for example). In addition, IP addresses are prone to change as underlying infrastructure changes, leading services to use ad-hoc sharing mechanisms like
CIDR lists
.Â

43994779.article_summary:
本文讨论了在AI代理流量增加的背景下，如何区分合法爬虫和恶意机器人。传统上，Cloudflare依靠用户代理头和IP地址验证爬虫身份，但这些方法存在易被伪造和不准确的问题。为了解决这一问题，文章提出了两种新的认证机制——HTTP消息签名和请求mTLS，以帮助友好机器人验证自身身份。

现有方法的问题包括：用户代理头易被伪造，IP地址共享和变化频繁，以及每个网站单独共享秘密（如Bearer token）不切实际。新机制利用加密技术，使机器人开发者能够对其服务发出的请求进行加密签名，从而使像Cloudflare这样的反向代理能够验证请求来源，帮助网站所有者更好地管理流量。

HTTP消息签名是一种标准化的请求加密认证方式，使来源能够确认发送者身份。请求mTLS则通过双向TLS验证实现更强的安全性。文章还邀请开发者参与其封闭测试。

data.title: Databricks acquires Neon
data.author: davidgomes
data.article_summary: Databricks宣布收购Neon，一家以开发者优先的无服务器Postgres公司。Neon团队开发了一种新的数据库架构，具有快速、弹性扩展以及分支和分叉功能，特别适合开发者和AI代理的需求。Neon的创始团队由Postgres专家组成，他们重新设计了数据库架构，实现了存储和计算的真正分离。Neon的快速数据库实例创建、自动化扩展和分支功能不仅提升了开发者体验，也适合AI代理的大规模使用。收购后，Databricks将与Neon共同提供开放的无服务器数据库平台，支持开发者和AI代理在现代化环境中的需求。两家公司都重视开源和技术创新，这构成了合作的基础。
data.comments_summary:

• 反对与担忧态度：

  - [crowcroft] 认为这次收购可能是 Databricks 的防御性举措，以应对越来越多的小公司选择简单 Postgres 复制方案而不是复杂的数据砖解决方案。

补充讨论：
• 一些用户（如 [Robdel12]）对个人职业影响的担忧，提到连续经历三次公司收购，因此更希望职业稳定。
• 一些用户（如 [aynyc]）分享了对 Databricks 产品从最初的好体验到后来无法满足公司需求的转变过程，表达了对 Databricks 逐渐变得像 Oracle 一样沉重的不满。
• 技术讨论中，用户提到了多种数据库和工具的比较，如 AWS RDS、Aurora、CockroachDB、Yugabyte 等，以及自建 PostgreSQL 方案的维护负担（[kjuulh]）。

• 对 AI 代理在数据库创建中的角色变化表示担忧，认为 Databricks 试图将 Postgres 包装成 AI 解决方案的趋势有问题。

Summary
We’re excited to announce that we have agreed to acquire
Neon
, a developer-first serverless Postgres company
The Neon team engineered a new database architecture that offers speed, elastic scaling, and branching and forking. The capabilities that make Neon great for developers are also great for AI agents
Together, we'll deliver an open, serverless database foundation for developers and AI agents
Today, we are excited to announce that we have agreed to acquire
Neon
, a developer-first, serverless Postgres company. Neon’s co-founders are among the very few people in the world who could re-architect Postgres with true separation of storage and compute, built for modern developers and AI systems. Their world-class team of Postgres hackers and database veterans will join Databricks to deliver serverless Postgres at production scale to developers in an AI-native world.
A developer-first mission, born from Postgres expertise
Four years ago, the Neon co-founders joined together with a vision to disrupt the database industry. They observed that the foundations of database technologies were largely designed for the 90s era. Their goal was to build a new database platform that would dramatically improve experiences for developers, in some fundamental ways:
They foresaw that Postgres would become the de facto standard for databases and had the vision to create a serverless Postgres platform.
They were determined to make it possible to create a new Postgres instance in seconds, so developers wouldn’t need to wait.
They set out to simplify the operational aspect of database scaling by automating it as load changed, so developers could start very small and not worry about over- or under-provisioning.
They wanted to enable rapid experimentation and testing by supporting instant forking and branching of databases and creating fully isolated databases, as databases are often one of the most difficult modules to test in end-to-end application testing.
A few years in, the Neon team engineered a new, innovative database architecture that decouples storage scaling from compute scaling, which ultimately enabled all of the above goals. When Neon first launched, developers raved about the speed, the simplicity, and the ability to branch and fork their databases like Git does for code.
The shift toward AI agents
As Neon became GA last year, they noticed an interesting stat: 30% of the databases were created by AI agents, not humans. When they looked at their stats again recently, the number went from 30% to over 80%. That is,
AI agents were creating 4 times more databases versus humans
.
If you think of AI agents as your own massive team of high-speed junior developers (potentially “mentored” by senior developers), it’s then not surprising that the same capabilities the Neon team focused on that made Neon great for developers also made Neon great for these AI agents:
Postgres open source ecosystem
: All frontier LLMs have been trained on the vast amount of public information available about the Postgres open source ecosystem, so all AI agents are experts in using Neon, which is built on Postgres.
Speed
: Traditional databases were designed for humans to provision and operate. It was OK to take minutes to spin up a database. Given AI agents operate at machine speed, ultra rapid provisioning time becomes critical.
Elastic scaling and pricing:
The decoupled storage from compute serverless architecture enables extremely low-cost Postgres instances. It’s now possible to launch thousands or even millions of agents with their own databases cost-effectively.
Branching and forking
: AI agents can be non-deterministic, and “vibes” need to be checked and verified. Neon’s ability to instantly create a full copy of a database, not only for schema but also for the data, allows all these AI agents to be operating on their own isolated database instance in high fidelity for experimentation and validation.
Shared DNA
We have long known Nikita Shamgunov, Heikki Linnakangas, and Stas Kelvich – the founders of Neon. Before Neon, Nikita started his career working on SQL Server and later became well-known in the database community as a co-founder and CEO of SingleStore, driving the startup’s business to over $100M in annual revenue. Heikki has been a committer on Postgres for two decades - he started his Postgres journey when he was bored on paternity leave and decided to look into Postgres internals for fun. Stas is an ex-physicist who got into Postgres hacking because he needed a better R-tree implementation for his tourism search engine startup.
Databricks and Neon share the same DNA in building hardcore technical innovations at the infrastructure layer. We also share the belief in the importance of open source: we originally started the Apache Spark™ project at UC Berkeley, which also happens to be the original birthplace of Postgres, the open source database project Neon builds

data.title: Clearly Incorrect
data.author: surprisetalk
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了名厨戈登·拉姆齐在制作烤奶酪三明治视频中的失误以及他关于牛排烹饪的错误建议。作者指出，尽管拉姆齐是一位杰出的厨师，但他有时会给出不准确的建议，例如让牛排在烹饪前放置十分钟，而这并未带来明显的好处。文章进一步探讨了这种现象背后的原因，认为许多专家在不重视真相的情况下给出建议，导致错误信息广泛传播，不仅限于烹饪领域，还包括医学和教育等行业。这种不准确的信息传播会对社会产生不良影响。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：评论围绕多个主题展开，包括真理的模糊性、信息传递的有效性、社会动态中的欺骗与合作，以及专家与娱乐的界限。

不同观点：
• **关于真理的模糊性**：有评论指出，在认识论上，信息并不总是简单的真或假，有时真理是模糊的。主观体验可能导致某些信息对个人为真，而对其他人不为真。语言作为沟通工具是不完美的，信息在传递过程中可能会失真。例如，某人可能意图传达讽刺，但被他人理解为权威性言论。

• **关于社会动态与欺骗**：评论提到，社会中存在类似于“反向囚徒困境”的现象，合作虽然理想但困难，而个人可能通过欺骗获得利益。某些情况下，出于谨慎、尊严或社会凝聚力等原因，歪曲或省略真相可能是正面的。例如，Gordon Ramsay的烹饪娱乐节目就是一种“让你愿意被欺骗”的例子。

• **关于传统建议与结果**：有人认为，即使某些建议的理论基础不正确，最终结果可能仍然较好。例如，Kenji对牛排内部温度的测试并没有直接衡量最终的口感，可能存在其他机制影响结果，如表面湿度等。

• **关于专家与娱乐的界限**：有评论指出，Gordon Ramsay等娱乐型专家首先是娱乐者，他们的首要任务是娱乐大众。虽然他们分享了很多准确的建议，但当准确性和娱乐性发生冲突时，他们往往选择后者。这种现象在职场中也存在，一些凭借魅力和娱乐性获得晋升的人可能并不具备真正的专业能力。

• **关于不同领域中的误导性建议**：有人提到，烹饪中的误导性建议（如煎牛排的方法）影响较小，但在自卫或武术等领域，重复传统但错误的建议可能更加危险。

• **关于编程领域的误导性信息**：有评论将讨论引申到编程领域，提到《Clean Code》这本书被许多初级开发者奉为圭臬，但其中包含的代码实践并不总是最佳的。

• **关于传统知识与个人认知**：有评论嘲讽那些质疑传统知识的人，认为这些人是“怪胎”，并举例说明一些明显的事实（如月亮与昼夜周期无关）来反讽。

补充讨论：
• **具体示例的对比**：有人认为Ramsay的某些视频（如炒鸡蛋）是完美的，而其他视频（如烤奶酪）则可能是“ bullshit”，这显示出对同一人的不同作品存在不同评价。

• **技术细节的讨论**：有评论提到某网站通过动态调整HTML元素的font-size属性来抵抗缩放，但最终还是被Firefox的阅读模式攻克，显示出技术实现与用户体验之间的博弈。

争议的焦点：
• 主要集中在真理的模糊性与信息传递的有效性上，以及专家角色中娱乐与专业性的平衡问题。这些讨论反映了人们对信息、知识和专家意见的多维度思考。

* * *
Clearly Incorrect
Gordon Ramsay is a funny guy. Sometimes, this humor is intentional. Most of the time it’s not. Four years ago, he posted a
grilled cheese sandwich recipe
video in which he somehow managed to burn the edges of the bread without (seemingly) even warming up the cheese inside. It’s one of the worst grilled cheeses I have ever seen.
“Oh my god… Goodness me… Oh my god, that’s incredible,” Ramsay says, as he bites into a sandwich that would have gotten someone fired on
Kitchen Nightmares
.
Chef Ramsay must know this is a bad grilled cheese. He is not an idiot. On paper, Ramsay is one of the great living chefs. His restaurants have garnered 18 Michelin stars. So you kind of wonder how the grilled cheese thing happened.
I can take a baseless guess: there was a tight shooting schedule, they rushed through it, and Ramsay thought, What the hell, just ship it. Who cares? It’s grilled cheese.
There’s another Gordon Ramsay-ism that I find less funny and more frustrating:
Take your steak out of the fridge at least 10 minutes before cooking it
. You may have heard this advice because there are leagues of skilled professional chefs who repeat it.
But why does Ramsay tell you to take your steak out of the fridge? The justification, in
this video
and
this article
, is that the steak needs to warm up so that you get a better sear and more even cooking. It makes sense if you don’t think very hard about it.
The truth is that Ramsay’s steak advice is total bullshit.
J. Kenji Lopez-Alt, a chef and food writer, put Ramsay’s (and others’) wisdom to the test. The even cooking rationale is plain wrong: a steak’s interior barely warms up at room temperature, even after
hours
of resting. And the searing justification is inaccurate, too, because that’s not actually how the physics of searing a steak work (
read Kenji’s piece
for the more detailed explanation).
So why does Ramsay keep giving this clearly incorrect advice? And why do people believe it?
* * *
Some people may read the above and think:
Gordon Ramsay is stupid. He’s actively trying to mislead people. He’s a terrible chef. Liar!!
But that’s a lazy interpretation, and one that is not well-calibrated with reality. Ramsay is probably not horrible. Rather, the unappetizing grilled cheese and bad steak advice stem from a problem that is present in almost all of us:
not really prioritizing the truth.
Philosopher
Harry Frankfurt
described “bullshit” as
“speech intended to persuade without regard for truth. The liar cares about the truth and attempts to hide it; the bullshitter doesn’t care whether what they say is true or false.”
This is the category that Gordon Ramsay’s steak wisdom falls into. He probably just doesn’t care that much about being accurate (or at least not as much as other priorities). And that’s why he’s okay saying some bullshit.
Not prioritizing the truth has a much worse impact on society than might be obvious.
Take the steak scenario. Ramsay, by all accounts an
expert
chef, gives a piece of advice to millions of people. Many of those people blindly trust in his advice. They don’t stop to verify it. Why would they? He’s the Gordon Ramsay. He has a British accent! The chain of blind trust extends to more than just regular people, too: culinary school instructors give advice to chefs, chefs give advice to other chefs. Only when someone takes the time to investigate are holes in the chain exposed.
Okay, the whole world makes bad steak. What’s the big deal?
Well, this problem extends
beyond
cooking myths.
Doctors frequently prescribe antibiotics (and tell patients they will work!) before they have confirmed that antibiotics are the right thing to prescribe. This is professional bullshit, and
up to 43% of antibiotic prescriptions
in the United States are inappropriate.
Physical therapists may tell you that you need to put ice on injuries. The truth is that
ice slows the body’s response
and likely delays the healing of muscle injuries. The doctor who coined the term RICE—rest, ice, compression, and elevation—
renounced his support
of the regimen in 2014 because of this fact. And yet millions of doctors and therapists still give incorrect advice.
Teachers often obsess over ‘learning styles’ in children, even though
our current understanding
of the topic is that traditional learning style wisdom is pretty useless.
Startup founders, and maybe all of your coworkers, repeat “best practices” they read about online (i.e. Google did OKRs, we need them too!) many times with no real justification beyond Other X Company Did This So We Should Too.
This list could be much longer—most “
experts
”, in every industry, say some amount of bullshit. They say things that are clearly incorrect, things that can be proven wrong in 10 seconds. They don’t bother fixing their bullshit because trustworthiness is not their highest priority. You probably spew bullshit too. It’s just that you’re not famous, and so it may even be harder to be hel
43953603.article_summary: 本文讨论了名厨戈登·拉姆齐在制作烤奶酪三明治视频中的失误以及他关于牛排烹饪的错误建议。作者指出，尽管拉姆齐是一位杰出的厨师，但他有时会给出不准确的建议，例如让牛排在烹饪前放置十分钟，而这并未带来明显的好处。文章进一步探讨了这种现象背后的原因，认为许多专家在不重视真相的情况下给出建议，导致错误信息广泛传播，不仅限于烹饪领域，还包括医学和教育等行业。这种不准确的信息传播会对社会产生不良影响。
43953603.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：评论围绕多个主题展开，包括真理的模糊性、信息传递的有效性、社会动态中的欺骗与合作，以及专家与娱乐的界限。

不同观点：
• **关于真理的模糊性**：有评论指出，在认识论上，信息并不总是简单的真或假，有时真理是模糊的。主观体验可能导致某些信息对个人为真，而对其他人不为真。语言作为沟通工具是不完美的，信息在传递过程中可能会失真。例如，某人可能意图传达讽刺，但被他人理解为权威性言论。

• **关于社会动态与欺骗**：评论提到，社会中存在类似于“反向囚徒困境”的现象，合作虽然理想但困难，而个人可能通过欺骗获得利益。某些情况下，出于谨慎、尊严或社会凝聚力等原因，歪曲或省略真相可能是正面的。例如，Gordon Ramsay的烹饪娱乐节目就是一种“让你愿意被欺骗”的例子。

• **关于传统建议与结果**：有人认为，即使某些建议的理论基础不正确，最终结果可能仍然较好。例如，Kenji对牛排内部温度的测试并没有直接衡量最终的口感，可能存在其他机制影响结果，如表面湿度等。

• **关于专家与娱乐的界限**：有评论指出，Gordon Ramsay等娱乐型专家首先是娱乐者，他们的首要任务是娱乐大众。虽然他们分享了很多准确的建议，但当准确性和娱乐性发生冲突时，他们往往选择后者。这种现象在职场中也存在，一些凭借魅力和娱乐性获得晋升的人可能并不具备真正的专业能力。

• **关于不同领域中的误导性建议**：有人提到，烹饪中的误导性建议（如煎牛排的方法）影响较小，但在自卫或武术等领域，重复传统但错误的建议可能更加危险。

• **关于编程领域的误导性信息**：有评论将讨论引申到编程领域，提到《Clean Code》这本书被许多初级开发者奉为圭臬，但其中包含的代码实践并不总是最佳的。

• **关于传统知识与个人认知**：有评论嘲讽那些质疑传统知识的人，认为这些人是“怪胎”，并举例说明一些明显的事实（如月亮与昼夜周期无关）来反讽。

补充讨论：
• **具体示例的对比**：有人认为Ramsay的某些视频（如炒鸡蛋）是完美的，而其他视频（如烤奶酪）则可能是“ bullshit”，这显示出对同一人的不同作品存在不同评价。

• **技术细节的讨论**：有评论提到某网站通过动态调整HTML元素的font-size属性来抵抗缩放，但最终还是被Firefox的阅读模式攻克，显示出技术实现与用户体验之间的博弈。

• 主要集中在真理的模糊性与信息传递的有效性上，以及专家角色中娱乐与专业性的平衡问题。这些讨论反映了人们对信息、知识和专家意见的多维度思考。

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：通过Wikipedia发现电影的方式及其相关问题

不同观点：
• **hasbot**：建议增加按语言过滤的功能，以提高发现电影的效率和个性化体验。

• **bad_username**：提出批评界的赞誉与个人对电影质量的感受不一定相关，尤其在过去十年中，批评界的评价与自己认为的“最佳电影”之间存在负相关。这表明依赖批评界的评价来选择电影可能并不总是有效。

• **sorokod**：提供了一个相关的例子，即《美国对国外语言电影的20个最佳翻拍》，并指出原版电影可能不为人知。这暗示了通过Wikipedia可以发现一些不为人知的优秀翻拍电影。

• 讨论中的一个争议焦点在于通过Wikipedia发现电影的有效性和准确性，尤其是依赖批评界评价是否能真正找到“最佳”电影。

data.title: RPG in a Box
data.author: skibz
data.article_summary: RPG in a Box 是一款简单有趣的游戏制作工具，无需编程或建模知识即可使用。它包含体素编辑器（用于创建和动画3D像素物件）、地图编辑器（用于构建网格世界并添加互动元素）、视觉脚本系统（通过拖放实现事件和对话）、自定义UI、基本物品定义以及声音生成器等功能。用户可以将自己的故事和创意转化为游戏，并导出为Windows和MacOS可独立运行的格式。此外，用户还可以加入官方论坛，参与社区交流与软件开发跟踪。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕RPG in a Box和相关工具、技术实现的讨论

不同观点：
• chrismorgan认为使用GIF导致了性能问题，建议用视频格式替代以提高加载速度和播放流畅度。他通过技术分析指出GIF格式在色彩和速度上的局限性。
• thomasfl从用户体验角度出发，强调RPG in a Box通过故事驱动吸引了他的儿子对编程的兴趣，指出编程只是实现故事创作的工具，而非目的。
• freetime2对RPG in a Box的图形风格持保留意见，更偏好像素艺术风格的RPG Maker，但同时认可RPG in a Box社区展示中的一些沉浸式创作。他建议在主页上更多展示社区创作以吸引用户。
• Buttons840简要提到RPG in a Box基于Godot引擎，提供了一个技术背景。
• dang提供了一个相关讨论的链接，指向之前关于RPG in a Box的讨论。
• hungryhobbit强烈反对在个人项目中自定义编程语言，认为这将导致项目长期支持不足，最终失败。
• 90s_dev对类似游戏引擎项目感到兴奋，认为这能激励其他开发者，并期待自己的项目发布。
• jamalaramala称赞RPG in a Box项目，并建议如果作者考虑开源，可以参考Blender的开放经验。
• goodboyjojo作为用户分享了自己的体验，表示曾经在Steam上购买并享受使用该软件。
• braggerxyz认为RPG in a Box与Godot相似，因此更倾向于使用Godot，但对RPG in a Box减少创作摩擦的特性表示认可。
• q2dg简短表示没有开源就没有乐趣，强调开源的重要性。
• the_real_cher用幽默的方式指出这个项目并非快速扩张的创业项目。
• Rooster61提到项目可能因为访问量过大而崩溃。
• qmr好奇RPG in a Box与RPGMaker的比较。
• khazhoux对现代有类似于Adventure Construction Set的工具表示高兴，认为这种理念曾丢失了几十年。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点之一是自定义编程语言的可行性，hungryhobbit认为这会拖累项目，而jamalaramala则建议开源以促进项目发展。
• 图形风格和工具选择也是讨论的重点，freetime2和braggerxyz对像素艺术和Godot有偏好，但都认可RPG in a Box的社区和创作潜力。
• 技术实现上，chrismorgan对GIF格式的问题提出了具体的技术解决方案。

43944199.article_content:
RPG in a Box lets you create games and other interactive experiences in a fun and simple way! But you don't have to take my word for it - see below for just a few words from the lovely community making so many wonderful things with it!
Interested in following the development of RPG in a Box? Have a question, suggestion, bug to report, or would just like to say hello? Click the banner above to join the official forum and be a part of the growing community!
RPG in a Box lets you easily turn your stories and ideas into games and other interactive experiences! As its name suggests, it contains everything necessary for doing so, all packaged together "in a box". The software is designed with a fun, beginner-friendly approach in mind as to not require any programming or modelling knowledge, while still providing a wide range of customization and openness. You can export your game to a standalone format for Windows and MacOS, allowing others to play it without needing to own RPG in a Box!
Voxel Editor:
Build tiles, objects, and characters from 3D pixel blocks (i.e. voxels) and easily animate them with the editor's frame-based, stop-motion animation system. Importing from MagicaVoxel (.vox) and Qubicle (.qb) is also supported.
Map Editor:
Create grid-based worlds with the tiles you've built, then bring them to life by adding interactive NPCs and objects using the editor's intuitive navigation and interaction system.
Visual Scripting:
Set up and trigger in-game events with the visual, node-based script editor. Simply drag and drop the desired actions (no programming knowledge required), or manually code "quick scripts" using the custom, Lua-like scripting language.
Dialogue:
Write conversations for your NPCs using a visual, flowchart approach similar to that of the script editor. Branching dialogue is supported via player choices and condition checking.
Camera System:
Choose from three available camera presets (standard, isometric, and first-person) or tweak the settings to create a custom camera. Stage dynamic cutscenes for your game using the engine’s flexible camera scripting system.
UI Customization:
Design one or more dialogue box themes and customize the appearance of many other interface elements such as the inventory, main menu, and credits roll.
Basic Items:
Define basic items for the player to find in containers or earn through the completion of tasks. Attach scripts to trigger effects for potions and other consumable items.
Sound FX Generator:
Generate fun, retro-style sound effects using the built-in tool based on Dr. Petter’s SFXR.

不同观点：
• [支持Fastmail] os2warpman和andyjohnson0都表示使用Fastmail超过十年，没有发现明显缺点。他们强调了使用自定义域名和良好的客户支持，同时提到Fastmail的稳定性和无广告体验。

data.title: SMS 2FA is not just insecure, it's also hostile to mountain people
data.author: todsacerdoti
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了居住在美国北卡罗来纳州山区的居民，尤其是老年人在使用短信双因素认证（SMS 2FA）时面临的困境。由于山区手机信号差，许多依赖SMS 2FA的网站无法向这些用户发送验证码，导致他们无法访问自己的账户。尽管可以使用Wi-Fi通话接收普通短信，但来自短代码的2FA短信通常不支持此功能。转换到基于时间的一次性密码（TOTP）2FA是一种解决方案，但需要技术知识和外部帮助。其他解决方案如更换VOIP服务或安装信号增强器成本高昂且不切实际。文章呼吁关注山区居民因手机信号差而在数字化生活中遇到的困难。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：通过不同方法解决手机信号差情况下接收SMS（特别是2FA验证码）的问题

不同观点：
• **VOIP和短码问题**：[lxgr]提到，将手机号转移到支持通过WiFi接收SMS的VOIP服务是一个解决方案，但有些公司不向VOIP号码发送SMS-OTP代码，或者要求号码“以她的名义注册”，而较小的运营商通常不这样做。

• **微型基站/家庭基站（Femtocell）**：[LeifCarrotson]建议使用微型基站，通过互联网连接提供蜂窝信号。这种设备可以直接从运营商获取，通常免费，但需要与运营商沟通。该方法解决了深山或信号盲区的问题，并且支持2FA代码接收。

• **SMS转发API**：[nelblu]分享了一种通过将SIM卡留在家中的备用手机上，并使用Android应用将SMS转发到API，然后通过电子邮件接收2FA代码的方案。这种方法特别适合国际漫游时使用。

• **Google Fi服务**：[modeless]推荐Google Fi服务，它能够在WiFi上接收所有SMS 2FA消息，包括短码，并且不需要手机开机。该服务起步价为20美元/月，且在部分山区也有良好覆盖。

• **TOTP与其他2FA方法的优缺点**：[stackskipton]指出SMS 2FA虽然安全性较低，但恢复容易且支持广泛。TOTP应用（如Google Authenticator）更安全，但手机丢失后恢复麻烦。Yubikey等硬件解决方案成本较高且也有恢复问题。有人提出政府运行集中式硬件认证系统的可能性，但因隐私问题在美国难以实现。

• **技术复杂性与用户体验**：[brettanomyces]和[swiftcoder]讨论了TOTP和PUSH验证的局限性，特别是TOTP在某些场景下无法使用，而PUSH验证需要为每个服务下载单独的应用，用户体验不佳。Passkeys作为新兴解决方案被提及，但其普及速度尚不确定。

补充讨论：
• **SMS接收不稳定**：[kaikai]提到自己生活在农村地区，依赖WiFi进行通话和SMS，但2FA代码的接收时好时坏，这种不一致性令人困惑。

• **WiFi专用运营商的设想**：[miki123211]提出了一种设想，即创建一个仅通过互联网提供服务的“WiFi专用运营商”，通过API或专有应用与用户通信。这种方法类似于SS7重定向攻击，但得到了用户的知情和同意。

• **具体设备推荐**：[vanburen]建议在至少有一个信号较好的区域时，使用4G路由器将SMS转发到电子邮件，这种方法虽然不理想，但对某些人来说可能是一个解决方案。

争议焦点：
• **SMS 2FA的安全性与便利性权衡**：部分用户（如[stackskipton]和[Calwestjobs]）认为SMS 2FA虽然便利，但存在安全隐患，特别是数据被用于营销目的。而TOTP和其他方法虽然更安全，但在用户体验和恢复方面存在问题。

• **运营商和技术限制**：不同用户提到运营商对VOIP号码、MVNO（移动虚拟网络运营商）和微型基站的支持不一，导致部分解决方案在实际应用中存在困难。

43984297.article_content:
SMS 2FA is not just insecure, it's also hostile to mountain people
May 14, 2025
i have a friend — she's an old lady born and raised here in the western north carolina mountains. she hates computers, yes, but she's been willing to learn a lot and quickly after joining a big signal group chat that our shared local community uses to keep in touch.
aside from memeing with the best of them in the group chat, she also maintains a large fish pond outside the house she built herself. this despite being in her 70s. she's an inspiration.
she has a landline. it works great, and the landline phone hardware works great with her hearing aids. she's had it for years. spectrum has a monoply in our area so the landline and her cable internet service is with spectrum.
she got a cell phone a few years ago. she got a smartphone basically because she had to to do basic life tasks, including joining the big signal group chat. at first she just used it on wifi, but quickly she decided she wanted to be able to use the phone everywhere so she got a cell phone plan from spectrum because they were already her ISP. spectrum mobile uses the verizon network — famed for its good rural coverage.
this is where things started to go haywire.
all her accounts on websites, things like email and bank accounts and health insurance and healthcare providers, they started trying to send her SMS messages in order to let her get into her accounts.
the SMS codes don't work, because they don't come. she doesn't have cell service at her house. it's up in the mountains, sure, but it's not
isolated
. she lives 20 minutes from downtown asheville and she has lots of neighbors on her road.
she turned on wifi calling on her phone. now she could receive SMS messages from friends and family, but 2FA codes still weren't coming through. i did some digging, and it turns out messages from 5 digit shortcodes often aren't supported over wifi calling. sometimes they are, but in her case they're clearly not. she has a current, stock iphone. she's using the spectrum-provided internet hardware. she knows how to use her phone.
i did more digging — it turns out some ISP-provided landline services support receiving SMS messages to the landline, and then a computer voice reads them out to you. “we don't offer that service” the spectrum chat told us.
some of these accounts can likely be converted to using TOTP 2FA rather than SMS 2FA. this is good, but you have to get in to begin with in order to turn that on. so what my friend has to do is:
make a list, over time, of the websites that she's locked out of because of SMS 2FA
not be able to use those sites at home the whole time she's making the list
schedule a meetup with a friend like me
drive to town to meet the friend
sit down and systematically go through the list of websites and convert them to TOTP
inevitably discover that some of them don't support TOTP
try and contact those companies and explain that they need to turn off SMS 2FA on her account so that she can use their healthcare/banking/email/whatever service from her home
discover that it's not possible to talk to a company anymore in 2025
other options available to her include
port her cellphone number to a VOIP provider that does support receiving SMS from shortcodes over wifi
spend hundreds of dollars setting up a cell tower signal booster outside her house
move
these are all ridiculous options that shouldn't be necessary in order to log in to a website.
if you look at the spectrum mobile coverage map where my friend lives, it shows she has perfect coverage at her house. and all her neighbors do too. all the way up the holler in fact!
this is simply false. she usually doesn't even have service 100 meters down the road.
another friend of mine who also lives out in the county, a millenial, once said that “SMS 2FA is the bane of [her] existence.” the valley she's in isn't even that deep.
and TOTP, the obvious alternative solution, is still pretty sorry. you have to download an app to do it, it's not just a capability that a phone has by default. and then when trying to find an app to use for it, you're presented with a multitude of high-stakes choices, and often pretty technical explanations if you start internet searching about which app to use.
i understand why SMS 2FA is so ubiquitous. when it works, the UX is good, nontechnical users intuitively understand it, and it's usually secure
enough
.
but there are 1.1
million
people in these western north carolina mountains, 25 million in the rest of the appalachians, and many millions more in the mountain west and pacific ranges.
we have internet, but we have F-tier cell service — what are we supposed to do?

data.title: Mipmap selection in too much detail
data.author: luu
data.article_summary:
这篇文章详细探讨了GPU在纹理采样时如何选择mipmap级别，以解决纹理锯齿问题。文章首先介绍了mipmapping的基本概念和用途，解释了纹理锯齿是由于屏幕像素覆盖的纹理区域大小不一导致的。通过生成一系列低分辨率的mipmap并应用低通滤波器，可以在纹理采样时选择合适的mipmap级别，从而减少锯齿现象。

文章进一步解释了像素导数（ddx()/ddy()）的作用，它们用于计算屏幕空间中变量的偏导数。这些导数可以帮助确定合适的mipmap级别，因为较大的导数通常对应于可能出现锯齿的情况。GPU会自动根据这些导数选择适当的mipmap级别，而无需在着色器中手动更改代码。

总的来说，文章揭示了GPU如何通过像素导数和mipmap技术自动选择合适的纹理分辨率，以优化图像质量并减少锯齿。

不同观点：

• [ahartmetz]：指出Adreno和AMD的名字关联（Adreno是Radeon的字母重组），并表示没有细读文章中的技术细节，但对这种技术关联感到有趣。
• [aeonik]：对文章中提到的“无法自己实现这些功能，因为它们是通过硬件实现的魔法内在机制”提出质疑，询问原因。
